title: The person's own machines over their own tailnet
description: Read and written by the person's daemon as the person: their own Tailscale node (a user unit), the devices Tailscale lists, and the machines in their SSH configuration. No field carries a key's private half, a node key or a credential; the login URL is Tailscale's own.

name.description: A device's name in the person's tailnet: the first label of its MagicDNS name.

user.description: The user on the machine whose rights the agent gets.

login.description: The tailnet account the node joined as.

shields_up.description: Inbound tailnet connections are refused. The node's locked config sets it; false means it was changed outside Habitat.

state.description: unavailable: this server ships no Tailscale; off: no node on the account; stopped: the node's unit exists but does not answer; login: waiting for the person's Tailscale login; approval: waiting for the tailnet's administrator; starting; on.

auth_url.description: Tailscale's own login page for this node, only while it waits for a login.

ssh.description: possible: macOS, Linux or Windows; no: a phone or other device without an SSH server.

machine.description: One machine in the person's SSH configuration (~/.ssh/config.d/habitat-<name>.conf); the agent reaches it with `ssh <name>`.

expires.description: The date the machine's line stops being accepted, as Habitat wrote it.

host_key.description: The pinned host key the person compared; empty when its file is gone.

connection_open.description: An SSH connection to it is open now (its control socket exists).

grant.description: The line for the machine and the command that installs it. Nothing is written on the account but the key, if it was missing.

shell.description: What the commands are for: sh on macOS and Linux, powershell on Windows (the machine's OS as Tailscale reports it).

command.description: Installs the line for the user: ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, on Windows %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\authorized_keys.

admin_command.description: Windows only: Windows' OpenSSH reads a member of Administrators' keys from %ProgramData%\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys; this installs the line there from an elevated PowerShell.

result.description: ok: the machine accepted the key and ran a command; key_rejected: it answered and refused the key; host_key_changed: a saved machine shows another host key; offline: Tailscale does not see it; no_ssh: nothing answers SSH on it; failed: anything else.

host_key.description: The host key the machine showed, for the person to compare before it is saved.

request.description: One action. A new machine is named only by its tailnet name; its address comes from Tailscale.

ssh_include.description: ~/.ssh/config includes the machines before its first Host block.

remove_command.description: Removes this account's line from a machine's authorized_keys.

windows_remove_command.description: The same in PowerShell on Windows.

windows_admin_remove_command.description: The same for an administrator on Windows, from an elevated PowerShell.
